title: A small x64 disassembler
description:
Combine the length decoder and the operand formatter of this milestone into a working disassembler for the common instructions of lesson 5.02, using a linear sweep:

```cpp
struct Line { std::uint64_t address; std::size_t length; std::string text; };

std::vector<Line> disassemble(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& code, std::uint64_t base);
```

Start at offset 0 and decode one instruction after another. Each `Line` has the instruction's address (`base` + offset), its length and its text. A byte that does not start a known instruction (or an instruction cut off by the end of `code`) becomes `db 0x0f` (two lowercase hex digits) with length 1, and decoding continues at the next byte. (Look at the test that does this: the bytes after an unknown instruction can decode as something plausible but wrong, exactly the weakness of linear sweep from lesson 5.02.)

**The subset.** An optional REX prefix (`40`-`4F`), then:

| Opcode | Text |
|---|---|
| `50`+r / `58`+r | `push r64` / `pop r64` (REX.B adds 8) |
| `C3`, `CC`, `90` | `ret`, `int3`, `nop` |
| `E8` / `E9` rel32, `EB` rel8 | `call TARGET` / `jmp TARGET` |
| `70`+cc rel8, `0F 80`+cc rel32 | `jCC TARGET` with cc names `o no b ae e ne be a s ns p np l ge le g` |
| `01 29 31 39 85 89` | `add sub xor cmp test mov` *rm*, *reg* |
| `03 2B 33 3B 8B` | `add sub xor cmp mov` *reg*, *rm* |
| `8D` | `lea` *reg*, *memory without the size keyword* |
| `83` /0 /4 /5 /7 ib | `add and sub cmp` *rm*, IMM (8-bit, sign-extended) |
| `81` /0 /4 /5 /7 id | the same with a 32-bit signed immediate |
| `C7` /0 id | `mov` *rm*, IMM (32-bit signed) |
| `B8`+r | `mov r32, IMM` (32-bit, unsigned); with REX.W `mov r64, IMM` (64-bit) |

**Formatting** follows lesson 5.02 and the practice of 5.02: operand size 64 with REX.W, else 32; register and memory operands exactly as `decodeModRm` produced them (`qword ptr [rbp-0x8]`, `[rip+0x10]`...). Immediates are `0x` plus lowercase hex, with `-` in front of negative ones (`-0x1`). Branch and call targets are absolute addresses: `0x` and lowercase hex of the address after the instruction plus the signed displacement. A ModRM `reg` field not listed for `83`, `81` or `C7` makes the instruction unknown.
hints: Write `decode(code, offset)` that returns either a finished `Line` or "not an instruction"; `disassemble` is then a loop that calls it and falls back to `db` for one byte. Keep a helper for each operand kind: register names, the ModRM operand (from the 5.02 practice), signed immediates and branch targets.
Every bounds check matters: a truncated instruction at the end of the buffer must become `db` bytes, never a read past the end.
requirements: Every instruction in the subset decodes to the right length and text.
Branch targets are absolute, computed from the instruction's own address.
Unknown bytes are shown as `db` and decoding resynchronises on the next byte.
A whole small function disassembles correctly from start to end.
stretch: Switch from linear sweep to recursive descent: start at offset 0, follow `jmp`, `jcc` and `call` targets that fall inside the buffer, stop each path at `ret` or `jmp`, and print the lines in address order with labels (`loc_1010:`) at every branch target.
